title: Add TP hang stress + fault-injection harness; integrate into CI and perf-canary
creator: Noah Patel
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Background
- We have production/staging incidents where TP worker groups enter a stuck state under sustained load (streaming + high concurrency), often with weak signals differentiating kernel stall vs comm stall vs scheduler deadlock.
- Fixes in this initiative (scheduler cancellation/barrier semantics, collective async error propagation, watchdog/quarantine) need a deterministic-ish way to reproduce and then prevent regressions.

Goal
- Introduce a stress + fault-injection harness that can reproduce the most common TP hang signatures with high probability.
- Wire the harness into:
  1) CI (PR-level gating for a small/fast subset), and
  2) perf-canary (nightly + pre-release runs with artifacts and alerts).

Scope (this ticket)
1) Harness / scenario runner
- Add a scenario runner (CLI) that drives the Redwood inference runtime with configurable load patterns while injecting controlled TP faults.
- Supported traffic patterns (v1):
  - Overload pattern: constant arrival rate above sustainable throughput to force backpressure + long queues
  - Mixed sequence lengths: p50 short prompts + p95 long prompts to stress fairness and barrier interactions
  - Streaming churn: high rate of client disconnects/cancels mid-generation
  - Burst pattern: N-second bursts with idle periods (to expose lifecycle issues / stale state)

2) Fault injection knobs (v1)
- Forced rank delay: artificially delay one TP rank on specific steps (e.g., every K tokens, or at prefill vs decode boundary) to simulate stragglers.
- Forced cancel: cancel requests at controlled points:
  - during prefill
  - during decode (after token i)
  - during streaming response write
- Optional (if time permits): forced collective error simulation (synthetic error surfaced to scheduler path) to validate propagation behavior without requiring NCCL/driver manipulation.

3) Detection + pass/fail criteria
- “Hang” definition:
  - No forward progress for a TP group for > T seconds (T configurable; default aligned with watchdog thresholds under test), OR
  - Collective call exceeds timeout threshold without surfacing error to scheduler, OR
  - Requests exceed end-to-end timeout with no progress counters.
- Required signals collected per run:
  - per-rank progress counters (from ENG-2404)
  - collective latency histograms / p99
  - watchdog trigger + quarantine counters
  - scheduler queue depth + active TP groups
  - error classification summary (comm stall vs kernel stall vs starvation vs canceled)
- Required artifacts:
  - structured logs for stall detection windows
  - scenario config used for the run
  - summary report (JSON + human-readable)

4) CI + perf-canary integration
- CI (fast subset):
  - Run 1–2 scenarios on a small multi-GPU executor (where available) or simulated fault mode if GPUs not available.
  - Hard fail on detected hangs/timeouts, or on >X watchdog triggers per scenario (X tuned to avoid flakes).
- Perf-canary (nightly):
  - Full scenario matrix on dedicated canary pool.
  - Publish run summary + links to artifacts, page/alert only on sustained regressions (e.g., 2 consecutive nightly failures).

Non-goals
- Not attempting to create a fully deterministic reproduction of NCCL-level deadlocks; focus is on probabilistic reproduction with good diagnostics.
- Not replacing benchmark-lab throughput benchmarks; this is a reliability/stall suite.

Acceptance criteria
- Harness exists as a first-class repo component with documented usage:
  - `tp_stress_runner --scenario <name> --duration <s> --concurrency <n> ...`
- At least 3 scenarios merged and runnable end-to-end:
  1) overload + mixed seq lengths
  2) streaming churn + forced cancel
  3) rank delay fault injection (prefill + decode variants)
- Each scenario produces artifacts (logs + summary report) and returns non-zero exit on hang detection.
- CI gating:
  - minimal scenario(s) run on PRs touching runtime scheduler/collectives (path-based or label-based trigger is OK)
  - flake rate <2% over 1 week (tracked in perf-canary/CI dashboards)
- Perf-canary:
  - nightly workflow runs the full suite and alerts on stall regressions
  - runbook link included in canary alert payload

Links
- Confluence spec: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/tp-hang-repro-stress-suite.json
- Initiative umbrella: ENG-2401
- Related work:
  - ENG-2403 (cancellation/barrier deadlock fix)
  - ENG-2404 (instrumentation: per-rank progress + collective latency)

Implementation notes / plan
- Week 1:
  - Implement scenario config + runner skeleton, artifact emission, and basic hang detection based on progress counters.
  - Land 1 scenario (overload + mixed lengths) in "informational" mode (no gating) to validate signal quality.
- Week 2:
  - Add fault injection hooks (rank delay + cancel) with deterministic triggers.
  - Integrate into perf-canary and start nightly runs.
- Week 3:
  - Add CI gating for minimal scenarios once flake rate is acceptable.
  - Document debugging workflow + common failure signatures.

Risks / mitigations
- Flaky failures due to noisy shared GPU environments:
  - Use a dedicated canary pool for nightly; for CI use smaller durations and thresholded alerts.
- False positives from overly sensitive hang detection:
  - Require "no progress" from multiple signals (e.g., progress counters + scheduler heartbeats) before failing.
- Maintenance overhead:
  - Keep scenarios small + composable; prefer config-driven patterns over ad-hoc scripts.
comments: 2025-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted runner interface and scenario schema. Plan is YAML/JSON scenario definitions + a single binary/CLI wrapper. Need final decision on artifact format (leaning JSON summary + log bundle).

2025-02-19 (Marcus Reed): +1 on config-driven scenarios. Suggest we standardize on a single “stall detector” implementation used by both CI and perf-canary to avoid divergence. Also, define an explicit progress signal: tokens_emitted_total and collective_steps_total per TP group.

2025-02-20 (Sofia Ivanova): For cancellation scenarios, please ensure we hit the problematic window: cancel during barrier wait and cancel during streaming disconnect while decode in-flight. We should parameterize cancel timing relative to prefill/decode boundary (e.g., cancel after first token).

2025-02-21 (Omar El-Sayed): For artifact collection, include structured log markers around: request enqueue, TP group assignment, collective begin/end, watchdog tick, quarantine start/end. This will make correlation much faster in post-run triage.

2025-02-24 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented v0 runner + scenario parsing; added overload + mixed-length scenario. Hang detection currently uses “no change in per-rank progress counters for 30s” and “no requests completed for 60s”. Still tuning thresholds to avoid classifying legitimate long-prefill as a hang.

2025-02-26 (Julian Moore): Instrumentation dependency: per-rank progress counters landed behind feature flag in ENG-2404 branch; please gate scenarios on that flag to avoid silent pass. I can help wire up metrics export to the runner output if needed.

2025-02-28 (Sahana Iyer): Added fault injection for forced cancel (client-side disconnect) and forced rank delay (sleep injected at token boundary) in test mode. Rank-delay scenario reproduces scheduler starvation + barrier wait in ~30–40% of runs on staging A100 pool; improving reproduction probability by increasing concurrency + mixed seq lengths.

2025-03-03 (Sahana Iyer): Opened PRs to wire into benchmark-lab + perf-canary. Nightly runs will publish a JSON summary + link to log bundle. Proposed alert: page only if 2 consecutive nights fail or if failure rate >20% across matrix.

2025-03-05 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure paging thresholds are conservative initially. For oncall usability, include a one-line classification in the alert (comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation) and a direct link to the debugging playbook section for that signature.

2025-03-06 (Sahana Iyer): Marking In Review. CI gating is staged: first week informational, then flip to required check for runtime scheduler/collectives paths once flake <2%. Remaining TODO: document local repro instructions and add a short “expected runtime + resource requirements” note.
